cards.q: What is LTE/5G cellular as a WAN transport?
cards.a: A wireless WAN transport ideal for primary in rural areas, backup, or roaming/merchant sites. It uses a SIM + APN on a cellular interface, gets IP via DHCP/static, and shines as an SD-WAN transport for automatic failover.

cards.q: Why choose LTE as a WAN link?
cards.a: Coverage works anywhere with signal, speed is LTE/5G, setup is simple with SIM + APN, it works on the move (mobility), and it requires no fixed wiring.

cards.q: What are the typical use cases for LTE?
cards.a: Primary for remote/rural sites, backup for failover, roaming for moving vehicles, and as an SD-WAN transport.

cards.q: What is the LTE interface model?
cards.a: A cellular interface such as Cellular0/0/0, identified by the SIM (subscriber identity), with an APN (provider access point) and a cellular profile configured for the carrier.

cards.q: What is the basic LTE interface configuration?
cards.a: Under interface Cellular0/0/0: ip address negotiated, cellular profile 1, no shutdown; plus a dialer-list (e.g. dialer-list 1 protocol ip permit) to trigger data.

cards.q: What does the cellular profile command do on an LTE interface?
cards.a: It sets the APN/access-point profile used to connect to the carrier.

cards.q: What are the characteristics of an LTE link?
cards.a: Moderate latency, variable bandwidth, data caps, variable predictability, and per-usage cost — so it must be treated as best-effort and metered.

cards.q: How does SD-WAN make LTE useful for failover?
cards.a: SD-WAN treats LTE as one of multiple transports, provides automatic failover, and can route by application via policy, making LTE a seamless automatic fallback.

cards.q: Which commands verify an LTE cellular link?
cards.a: show cellular 0/0/0 hardware, show cellular 0/0/0 radio, show cellular 0/0/0 profile, show interface Cellular0/0/0, and show ip interface brief.

cards.q: An LTE interface has no signal. What is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: Poor coverage is likely; check show cellular 0/0/0 radio.

cards.q: An LTE interface gets no IP address. What is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: An APN/profile problem is likely; check show cellular 0/0/0 profile.

cards.q: What identifies a device on an LTE/5G network?
cards.a: The SIM provides subscriber identity, and the APN/access profile connects it to the provider; the router itself uses serial number and cellular profile identity.
